title: ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Warming Up $83M+ 5-Day As Thanksgiving Stretch Box Office Sees $220M+ – Update
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Warming Up $83M+ 5-Day As Thanksgiving Stretch Box Office Sees $220M+ – Update David Byrne On Getting Into Character As Elon Musk For ‘Musk’ Song “Let Me Sell You A Dream” – Crew Call Podcast Takashi Miike’s ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ From Neon Sets Spring Release View All November 28, 2026 8:58am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Whitney Peak and Joseph Zada Lionsgate SATURDAY AM: The Thanksgiving five-day stretch for all movies is coming in at an estimated at $220M+ per sources, which isn’t the worst we’ve seen post Covid; higher than 2021, 2022 and 2023, but certainly far off as we always expected from 2024’s $424.9M (-48%) and even last year’s fifth best ever ($290.3M, -24%). Thank God for Lionsgate , Suzanne Collins and Francis Lawrence for resuscitating The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , which is now seeing a Wednesday-Sunday estimate of $83.5M , because Walt Disney Animation’s Hexed (with a $33M-$34M 5-day ) isn’t cutting it, and Universal/Paramount’s Ariana Grande-Ben Stiller-Robert De Niro Focker In-Law (coming in with $40.1M ) is more counter programming than event (which is still essential in the diversity of a box office marketplace). But any easing we’re seeing at the Thanksgiving box office will be made up greatly by the end of the year as Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers: Doomsday and Warner Bros/Legendary’s Dune: Part III shoot for the best weekend ever, potentially surpassing this year’s July 31-Aug 3 frame of $437.1M. Watch on Deadline FOCKER-IN-LAW , (aka FOCKER IN-LAW), from left: Robert De Niro, Skyler Gisondo, Ariana Grande, 2026. ph: Atsushi Nishijima / © Universal Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Focker In-Law in regards to domestic box office to budget, $40.1M opening to $90M production cost, should be fine before we start counting International which Paramount is handling. It’s slightly cheaper than the $100M of 2010’s Little Fockers, yet more expense than 2004’s Meet the Fockers $80M (unadjusted for inflation). Among the openings in the Meet the Parents franchise, Focker In-Law is third behind Meet the Fockers (amazing Christmas 5-day of $70.5M, $46.1M 3-day; that would be sweet to achieve those numbers on a purse comedy nowadays) and Little Fockers ‘ $45M 5j-day during Christmas 2010. Word of mouth on this movie was mixed according to RelishMix who weighed it at a 5.2 out of 10 on their buzz meter. While there’s a contingency that appreciate the gender flip of Ariana Grande in lead versus just being a retread, there’s another who yell “enough already” on social and that the franchise is akin to “beating a dead horse.” Grande, though clearly the draw here, is a double-edged sword per what RelishMix is seeing with some believing that they’re watching her versus playing another character in the film. HEXED, Billie (voice: Hailee Steinfeld), 2026. © Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Hexed is another Thanksgiving bomb for Walt Disney Animation following Wish ($31.6M 5-day) and Strange World ($18.8M). To think that 11 years ago, Disney got dragged over the underperformance of Pixar’s Good Dinosaur ($55.5M 5-day, $123M final domestic, $332M WW, $175M-$200M production cost), but at that box office threshold, it’s a hit. The movie, despite audiences enjoying it at an A-, is a tad out of season with its story of a mother-and-daughter witch, having a more Halloween feel than say Wicked (which is squarely rooted in the Wizard of Oz ). Not to mention, there’s no original songs to take this property to another atmopsheric level, rather non-fresh needle drops, i.e. Dua Lipa’s six-year-old “Levitating” and The Car’s 42-year old song “Magic”. Hailee Steinfeld can sing beautifully — why isn’t she singing throughout this entire movie? The industry can cry about how hard it is to launch original animated films, that streaming is butting in on the subgenre, however, history has shown that it’s possible to make a sublime, largely unique tale with compelling characters and emotional songs, i.e. Disney’s Frozen and Pixar’s Coco. RelishMix saw the lackluster word-of-mouth on social ahead of opening with “Mixed-negative leaning chatter for Hexed with the dominant complaint being structural vibes as viewers accuse the film of lifting The Owl House’s series skeleton while surgically removing its queerness. There’s a sharp sub-thread lamenting, ‘gender-swap of the lead from boy to girl.’ Comments accuse ‘the studio designed every shot for TikTok rather than the big screen’ while others compare the shift to a franchise precedent: ‘When I heard they changed the gender of the protagonist, all I could think of is how they destroyed Chicken Little by forcing a male protagonist years into the movie’s development.'” The social media universe reach for Hexed across TikTok, YouTube, X, Instagram and Facebook was OK, though not spectacular, with 400 million followers, which which is slightly higher than Universal/DreamWorks Animation’s original title Forgotten Island (382.8M followers), higher than Elemental (301M followers) and Wish (343.6M). More… A history of the Thanksgiving domestic marketplace: FRIDAY AM: Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping saw the second best Thanksgiving and Thursday of the franchise with $11.6M after Catching Fire ‘s $14.95M 13 years ago and ahead of Mockingjay Part 2 ‘s $11M in 2014. The running cume of the sixth feature adaptation of the Suzanne Collins series is $174.9M with an $85M 5-day still within reach. Yesterday, the fifth Francis Lawrence directed Hunger Games pic flew past the $166.3M lifetime cume its predecessor, 2023’s Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ‘ $166.3M. Sunrise on the Reaping ‘s running total by Sunday looks stand around $233M, which will be 17% ahead of Mockingjay 2 at the same point in time and +3% ahead of Mockingjay 1. Both titles respectively ended their domestic runs at $282M and $337.1M. The highest grossing Hunger Games title is Catching Fire with $425.3M. All pics at the Thanksgiving Box Office rang up an estimated $35.6M, -9% from last year’s Thanksgiving. Business is expected to go up to $59M on Black Friday, a busy moviegoing day — but it’s not going to be as busy as last year when all titles minted $75M, boosted by Zootopia 2 and Wicked for Good. Those who watched the part 2 of the Brad Pitt movie gave it an 88% on RT, which is very good and higher than Once Upon a Time in Hollywood ‘s 70% — it’s just not being found in a major way by male dudes. Theater average over 5-days is $14,880 still better than Wake Up Dead Man ‘s $7K a year ago. title: ‘His Weakest Creatures’ Director on Offering Hope to Egyptians With His Feel-Good Crime Comedy, Starring Ahmed Helmy and Hend Sabry
full_text: × Nov 28, 2026 8:24am PT ‘His Weakest Creatures’ Director on Offering Hope to Egyptians With His Feel-Good Crime Comedy, Starring Ahmed Helmy and Hend Sabry By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest ‘His Weakest Creatures’ Director on Offering Hope to Egyptians With His Feel-Good Crime Comedy, Starring Ahmed Helmy and Hend Sabry 1 hour ago ‘Clarissa’ Directing Duo on How Sophie Okonedo and Star-Studded Ensemble Brought Neon’s Lagos-Set ‘Mrs. Dalloway’ Adaptation to Life 1 hour ago Jessy Moussallem’s ‘Faux Bijoux,’ Laila Abbas’ ‘America Is Behind the Door’ Take Top Prizes at Marrakech’s Atlas Workshops 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source "His Weakest Creatures" (Courtesy Marrakech Film Festival) Egyptian filmmaker Omar Hilal (“Voy! Voy! Voy!”) unites two of the Arab film world’s most bankable stars in his latest feature, “His Weakest Creatures,” a dark comedic thriller that premiered with a gala screening Friday at the Marrakech Film Festival . Starring Egyptian comedian and actor Ahmed Helmy (“Wahed Tany”) and Tunisian screen icon Hend Sabry (“Four Daughters”), the film follows a desperate zoologist (Helmy) at Cairo’s crumbling Giza Zoo who agrees to sell animals to a wealthy buyer, pulling him into a dangerous smuggling operation that could save his family — or destroy everything he has spent his life protecting. Related Stories 'The Tree' Director Julie Bertuccelli Tells IFFI Masterclass a Canadian Producer Stole Her 'Italian Shoes' Adaptation, Readies India-Set Feature Australian Film Festival of India Returns After COVID-19 Pause, Launches Co-Production Bootcamps as Treaty Takes Effect (EXCLUSIVE) Co-written by the director and his brother Ahmed Hilal, the film is produced by Cairo-based Film Clinic and Dubai-based Front Row Filmed Entertainment — who previously collaborated on the local remake of “Perfect Strangers,” the first Arabic-language Netflix original — along with HWC Productions, Film Square, Arabia Pictures and Block 8, in association with Sinai Studios. Front Row is handling the film’s international sales. “His Weakest Creatures” was inspired by the incredible, pulled-from-the-headlines story of a spate of mysterious disappearances that took place at the Giza Zoo between 2005 and 2008, when an estimated 400 animals were stolen. As with the director’s previous effort, which represented Egypt in the 2024 Oscar race for best international feature, the film focuses on the travails of everyday Egyptians whose fortunes have steadily eroded, along with their hopes for returning their struggling nation to its former glory. But as with “ Voy! Voy! Voy! ,” a black comedy about a security guard who attempts to escape Egypt and his dead-end life by faking blindness, Hilal was determined not to make a downbeat drama — to, as he puts it, “paint those stories with a miserable brush.” Instead, he wanted to find the humor — and hope — in the story of the principled Ahmed and his determined wife Hala (Sabry), who are struggling to hold their precarious middle-class lifestyle together. In a country whose corrupt elites operate with impunity, the director says he wanted to tell a story where “the weak man wins,” adding: “We need that in Egypt. Because for years, for decades, people are just going on with their lives, but they’re not really living. “I found that in this story of thefts happening with the zoo, this ailing zoo, which was a wonder — it was called ‘the jewel of Africa’ — it was a perfect metaphor for Egypt,” he continues. “This place that was the center of everything in the Middle East. And we’ve lost that position.” The film’s title comes from the Egyptian proverb “God instills His secret in His weakest creatures.” Hilal describes the adage as “a way for the Egyptian man to find a way out,” clinging to the hope “that somehow, God’s going to save me.” The movie takes place in 2007, several years before successive revolutions, in 2011 and 2013, that briefly upended the status quo but “didn’t help create opportunity for the common Egyptian,” Hilal says. “On the contrary, the disparity between the rich and the poor has become much worse.” As a result, many Egyptians today feel oddly nostalgic for that era — what the director describes as “a time where you felt a certain safety in stagnation,” despite the rampant corruption that, he says, was pushing the country toward a boiling point. Born and raised in Cairo, Hilal knew he wanted to be a filmmaker since the age of 13. But his path to cinema took a lengthy detour, first as a TV director in Italy and later as an adman in Egypt, where he worked as a creative director for global advertising agency Leo Burnett. In 2022, he finally returned to his childhood dream, saying: “Seven, eight hundred commercials later, I made my first movie.” Upon its release “Voy! Voy! Voy!” was a box-office hit in Egypt and across the Middle East, later embarking on a festival tour that included stops in Marrakech and Rotterdam. Its global rights were picked up by AGC Studios, and with the movie attracting international recognition, Hilal eventually found himself sitting across a desk from a prospective manager in Hollywood. It was in the middle of their conversation that the director suddenly remembered a recent Facebook post he’d seen about the animal thefts in Cairo. “I’d just met the man,” he says. “And I told him, ‘Can you hold on one second? Because I have a very bad memory and I just thought of something.’ And I wrote down: zoo robbers.” Thus, a film was born. “His Weakest Creatures” is not only grounded in the bygone era of pre-revolution Egypt, but in the leafy Cairo suburb of Maadi, a neighborhood that Hilal says “is still holding on to its Egyptianness.” The director describes it as “the last fort” against the rampant consumerism that has overtaken so much of modern-day Egypt. “People who are from Maadi want to hold onto Maadi. They don’t want anything changed about it,” he says. “And that’s the way that I feel. I would love for the simpler Egypt to come back.” It’s a feeling that he wanted to evoke in “His Weakest Creatures,” a movie that’s grounded in “kindness,” he says. “It has to make you comfortable and feel like somebody’s giving you a hug.” The Marrakech Film Festival runs Nov. 20 – 28. ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2 ‘Gangs of London’ Director Kim Hong-sun Shoots Korean Martial Arts Action Film ‘The Hit List’ With Jung Woo-sung, ‘Squid Game’ Star Wi Ha-jun ‘Squid Game’ Creator Hwang Dong-hyuk Teases Possible Return to Franchise: ‘When I Have a Great Idea, I’ll Make Another One’ Loading comments...

title: ‘Clarissa’ Directing Duo on How Sophie Okonedo and Star-Studded Ensemble Brought Neon’s Lagos-Set ‘Mrs. Dalloway’ Adaptation to Life
full_text: × Nov 28, 2026 8:24am PT ‘Clarissa’ Directing Duo on How Sophie Okonedo and Star-Studded Ensemble Brought Neon’s Lagos-Set ‘Mrs. Dalloway’ Adaptation to Life By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest ‘His Weakest Creatures’ Director on Offering Hope to Egyptians With His Feel-Good Crime Comedy, Starring Ahmed Helmy and Hend Sabry 1 hour ago ‘Clarissa’ Directing Duo on How Sophie Okonedo and Star-Studded Ensemble Brought Neon’s Lagos-Set ‘Mrs. Dalloway’ Adaptation to Life 1 hour ago Jessy Moussallem’s ‘Faux Bijoux,’ Laila Abbas’ ‘America Is Behind the Door’ Take Top Prizes at Marrakech’s Atlas Workshops 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Neon It’s been a whirlwind year for Chuko and Arie Esiri , the breakout Nigerian directing duo whose star-studded, Lagos-set “Mrs. Dalloway” reinterpretation “Clarissa” wowed audiences at this year’s Cannes Film Festival. After premiering in the Directors’ Fortnight section of the prestigious French fest, the film set off on a lengthy festival run that’s included stops at the Toronto Intl. Film Festival and the New York Film Festival. It arrives this week in Marrakech, where it plays in the Horizons strand, ahead of a U.S. theatrical release by Neon on Dec. 11. Related Stories Rishab Shetty Wins Best Actor for 'Kantara: A Legend - Chapter 1' as Tiago Guedes' 'Aqui' Takes Golden Peacock at International Film Festival of India Barun Sobti, Abhishek Banerjee Star as 'Paatal Lok' Creator Sudip Sharma Swaps Violence for Black Comedy in Netflix's IFFI Selection 'Pushpak Vimaan' A reimagining of Virginia Woolf’s classic novel, “Clarissa” follows a society woman as she prepares to host a party at her home in Lagos, where she’ll unexpectedly encounter once-intimate friends from her youth. Reviewing the film in Cannes, Variety ’s Jessica Kiang heralded the Esiri duo’s “quietly dazzling Nigerian reinterpretation of ‘Mrs. Dalloway,’” praising “a superb Sophie Okonedo , radiant with melancholy, at the heart of its remarkably well-cast ensemble,” which includes David Oyelowo (“Selma”), India Amarteifio (“Queen Charlotte”), Ayo Edebiri (“The Bear”) and Toheeb Jimoh (“Ted Lasso,” “Industry”). “Expanding in ambition and feeling from their promising debut ‘ This Is My Desire ’ (aka ‘Eyimofe’),” wrote Kiang, “the Esiris cast a perceptive eye over the elite social constellation that has fallen into orbit around this dutiful but unfulfilled society wife, and have nothing but compassion for her as she spins slowly around and around at its center: loved by some, resented by others, admired by all — and totally alone.” The Esiri Brothers spoke with Variety in Marrakech a day after the film’s well-received regional premiere. Over Moroccan mint tea at the Es Saadi Palace, Chuko described his life-long love affair with Woolf’s groundbreaking novel, which depicts a single day in the life of a society woman in 1920s London. It was a book he revisited several years ago, he explained, during a particularly turbulent period for the brothers. “We had made a first feature, it had had a handful of rejections from festivals, Nigeria had had a really bad election,” he said, “and I was thinking a lot about choices, and where we were. “I think all of that was swimming within me. So I started looking at it and reading it and feeling the weight of the decisions we make, and how it’s just a collection of small decisions that lead to, like, ‘Fuck, is this it?’” He laughed. “It’s just a series of small things. It’s stunning. It’s staggering how that could happen.” David Oyelowo and Sophie Okonedo in “Clarissa” Courtesy of Neon, Cannes Film Festival On the surface, transposing a story set in post-WWI London to modern-day Lagos might seem like an unlikely fit, though the directors noted that many of the cultural norms of Nigerian high society were directly imported from the country’s former colonial rulers. “[Clarissa] is a very complicated person that’s hemmed in by tradition and society, and what the British idea of being civilized is,” said Chuko. “But at the same time, there’s this free person — this person that desires more than what she has, or believes that there’s more to life than everything that’s presented to her.” Arie added: “I think that translates to every culture, to every society.” “Mrs. Dalloway” masterfully depicted the richly imagined interior lives of her characters, a fact that doesn’t easily lend itself to adaptation for the big screen. Arie praised his brother for “extracting the drama in the book and divorcing himself…from the interior monologues of the characters, whittling it down to the essence of their being, or their presence within this day.” Chuko said his choices largely came down to “putting a lot of faith and trust in the audience,” adding, “and then, obviously, wonderful actors that could bring it out.” Chief among them is Okonedo, who dazzles in the lead role. During an audience Q&A after the film’s Marrakech screening, Arie recalled a conversation he had with the “Hotel Rwanda” actress once production was underway. “This is such an interior piece of work. How on earth are we going to externalize what’s happening within?” he asked her. Okonedo replied: “If I feel it, you will see it.” The brothers also credited Oscar-nominated casting director Nina Gold (“Game of Thrones”), who most recently led the search for the next James Bond, for piecing together “Clarissa’s” star-studded ensemble. “That foundation was really laid by Nina Gold,” said Arie. “She talked about casting for essence. She wasn’t so concerned about matching people’s physical attributes as opposed to their essence. That really set us up for success.” It certainly didn’t hurt to have a deep pool of acting talent to lean on, with Chuko noting that “it’s always been a dream for us to be a bridge between Nigeria and the diaspora.” Both the U.K.-born Okonedo and the American actress Edebiri trace their paternal roots to Nigeria; Oyelowo and Jimoh’s parents were both born in the West African nation, while Amarteifio is partly of Ghanaian descent. During the Marrakech Q&A, Chuko described how the brothers are “trying to expand the canvas of how Lagos and how Nigeria seem,” saying: “I feel there’s an expectation of what films from Africa should look like or feel like, and we wanted to go against that.” They’re certainly not alone, with Nigerian filmmakers like Cannes breakout Akinola Davies Jr. (“My Father’s Shadow”) and Sundance prizewinner C.J. Obasi (“Mami Wata”) cementing the country’s cinematic reputation on the world stage. For the Esiri Brothers, though, that rising generation of directors is just the foundation for where the industry must go from here. “I would really love it to spread beyond writers and directors and into artisans, the same way you had with Cha Cha Cha Films and [Alejandro González] Iñárritu and [Alfonso] Cuarón and [Guillermo] del Toro and the artisans they worked with,” said Chuko. “The DPs, the production designers. I think that’s the next step, to be able to have a pool of really great below-the-line talent that really will unlock it. “It’s a thing that we’ll see more of, in terms of Nigerian filmmakers playing at large festivals, and Nigerian films being programmed,” he continued. “The train is on that track. It’s now just a question of how you get beyond that space where it feels like it’s a small troupe of arthouse filmmakers. How do you make that more than just a small group of individuals?” “We need people to be interested in all aspects of the industry and hone their craft in all sorts of places and come back and make stuff,” added Arie. “Come back and work with us and collaborate.” The Marrakech Film Festival runs Nov. 20 – 28. ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2 ‘Squid Game’ Creator Hwang Dong-hyuk Teases Possible Return to Franchise: ‘When I Have a Great Idea, I’ll Make Another One’ ‘Gangs of London’ Director Kim Hong-sun Shoots Korean Martial Arts Action Film ‘The Hit List’ With Jung Woo-sung, ‘Squid Game’ Star Wi Ha-jun Loading comments...

title: Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival Opens With Lawrence Fajardo’s ‘Silenced Nights’ and a Call to Face Reality
full_text: × Nov 28, 2026 8:16am PT Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival Opens With Lawrence Fajardo’s ‘Silenced Nights’ and a Call to Face Reality By Jenny S. Li , Domi Eka Add us as a Google Preferred Source JAFF The 21st Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (JAFF) kicked off Nov. 28 at the Empire XXI cinema in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, with Filipino director Lawrence Fajardo’s thriller “Silenced Nights” as its opening film. The evening’s gentle drizzle stopped shortly after the ceremony began. Festival founder Garin Nugroho introduced this edition’s theme, “Influx,” which casts filmmakers in the ecosystem as surfers. “Together – you, us, and the guests – we are able to surf to keep cinema alive throughout this country,” Nugroho said. Related Stories Indian Feature 'Carretera Austral' Lines Up Chilean Partner for Southern Chile Shoot (EXCLUSIVE) Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki Remembered by Singer K.S. Chithra and Suhasini Maniratnam at IFFI's Lata Mangeshkar Talk The ceremony then took a political turn. Festival president Ifa Isfansyah and festival director Budi Irawanto invited the audience to reflect on the unsettling state of the world, pointing to natural and political crises and social inequality that threaten people’s safety. “A festival must not be a space separate from reality; it cannot just be a place to escape from problems out there. Instead, a festival must be a space to face reality, open up conversations, bring together various perspectives, and preserve the possibility of critical thinking,” said Irawanto, who then asked attendees to stand for a moment of silence. Fajardo thanked the festival and said the film is personally meaningful to him. “Silenced Nights,” set against extrajudicial killings in a Philippine urban community, played in the Platform competition at the Toronto International Film Festival in September. Indonesian singer Mondo Gascaro closed the night with a live set that opened with the soothing “Butiran Angin” and took in “Senandung Lagu Lama,” from Usmar Ismail’s 1956 musical “Tiga Dara” (“Three Maidens”); “Apatis,” composed for Nugroho’s “Kucumbu Tubuh Indahku” (“Memories of My Body”); and “Dan Bila.” The main competition includes two Cannes titles: Zou Jing’s “A Girl Unknown,” which won the Fipresci prize in Critics’ Week, and Sompot Chidgasornpongse’s Directors’ Fortnight selection “9 Temples to Heaven.” Also competing are Indonesian director Jeremias Nyangoen’s “Black Coffee” and Japanese animation “Cherry and Virgin.” A slate of non-screening events is open to the public. title: Rishab Shetty Wins Best Actor for ‘Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1′ as Tiago Guedes’ ‘Aqui’ Takes Golden Peacock at International Film Festival of India
full_text: × Nov 28, 2026 7:57am PT Rishab Shetty Wins Best Actor for ‘Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1′ as Tiago Guedes’ ‘Aqui’ Takes Golden Peacock at International Film Festival of India By Udita Jhunjhunwala Plus Icon Udita Jhunjhunwala Guest Contributor Latest Farhan Akhtar, Ashutosh Gowariker and Madhur Bhandarkar Look Back at ‘Dil Chahta Hai,’ ‘Lagaan’ and ‘Chandni Bar’ at 25 17 hours ago ‘Dangal’ Casting Director Mukesh Chhabra Recalls Auditioning Nearly 14,000 Girls, Shares Self-Tape Tips at IFFI Masterclass 1 day ago Barun Sobti, Abhishek Banerjee Star as ‘Paatal Lok’ Creator Sudip Sharma Swaps Violence for Black Comedy in Netflix’s IFFI Selection ‘Pushpak Vimaan’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source PIB Portuguese filmmaker Tiago Guedes’ Spanish-language film “Aqui” won the Golden Peacock for Best Film at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), which concluded in Goa on Nov. 28. Produced by Paulo Branco, “Aqui” received the festival’s top award, with the jury praising its ability to transport audiences into “a comforting and dreamlike universe that, despite its unpredictability, feels like one we belong to and don’t wish to leave.” The director and producer share the award and its INR5.1 million ($57,000) cash prize. Related Stories Ashutosh Gowariker Wants IFFI Goa to Be a First-Stop Festival for Filmmakers, Rules Out 'Lagaan' Sequel Australian Brothers Discover They Are Indian Cinema Royalty in WAVES Film Bazaar Documentary 'Dada & Us' Kannada cinema actor-director Rishab Shetty won the Silver Peacock for Best Actor (Male) for “Kantara: A Legend – Chapter 1,” which also received a Special Mention. German filmmaker Volker Schlöndorff was named Best Director for “Visitation,” while Maya O’Rourke won Best Actor (Female) for “The Meltdown.” The Silver Peacock for Best Debut Feature Film of a Director was awarded to Bérenger Thouin for “The Golden Age.” The jury commended the director’s vision in blending archival material with real footage to create an ambitious and compelling period film. Thouin’s brother Céleste, the film’s composer, accepted the award on the director’s behalf. The Silver Peacock for Special Jury Award went to Argentine film “The River Train,” directed by Lorenzo Ferro and Lucas A. Vignale. The ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal, which recognizes a film reflecting the ideals promoted by UNESCO and the values associated with Mahatma Gandhi, was awarded to “Rahma,” directed by Turkish filmmaker Faysal Soysal. Vishal Chaturvedi’s “Hanuman Ansh” won Best Debut Director of an Indian Feature Film. The jury praised the film for bringing together culture, faith and music with a strong emotional connection. The Best Web Series (OTT) award went to “Made in India: A Titan Story,” directed by Robbie Grewal. Its citation praised the story of “dreams realized and aspirations fulfilled across India.” The closing ceremony, held at the Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium, featured music and dance performances. Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting secretary Chanchal Kumar, festival director Ashutosh Gowariker and international jury chair Aanand L. Rai were among those present. Sawant also honored award-winning Goan filmmaker Aditya Suhas Jambhale. “When we speak about film festivals, we are really celebrating two simple things: the stories and strangers who turn into friends,” Sawant said in his address. Gowariker, reflecting on his first year as festival director, said his aim had been to push IFFI forward rather than repeat what had been done before. He acknowledged that the festival had not gotten everything right, said those experiences would serve as lessons, and thanked filmmakers and the people of Goa. “We laugh and cry together, and we feel the pain of someone miles away,” he said. Kumar spoke about IFFI’s place in the history of Indian cinema and its role in bringing Indian and international films together. “May the great next story that catches the world begin its journey from India,” he said. This edition screened more than 150 international films from 86 countries, with Spain as Country of Honor and Russia as Partner Country, alongside a BRICS showcase. title: Broadway Gets Speed-Dating-Style Tribute At Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Kicks Off, Making History On A Dry And Breezy Saturday ‘The Hunting Wives’ Pays Tribute To Lionsgate Exec Salli Newman Justin Timberlake Visits Jimmy Fallon And Shares Thanksgiving Dish On New Apple TV Doc Series, How David Bowie Influenced ‘SexyBack’ & Performs Dance Classics View All November 28, 2026 7:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jarrod Spector singing "You'll Be Back" from 'Hamilton' during the Macy's Parade Screen Capture The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade’s “ All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration ” went off without a hitch, even if it seemed more like a Broadway -themed speed-dating exercise. Nine musical productions – a mix of long-running shows and newcomers – were each given about a minute to show their stuff and pitch a nationwide audience on buying a ticket or two and taking in a Broadway show. Broadway’s big parade moment arrived at 9:13 a.m. ET, nearly 45 minutes into the event, with emcee Julianne Hough (soon to hit Broadway in Damn Yankees ) arriving with some formally clad backup dancers to stake a perch on a couch to watch the medley. Related Stories News Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Kicks Off, Making History On A Dry And Breezy Saturday News The Show Must Go On: Broadway Will Perform Saturday In Macy's Thanksgiving Parade The medley began with Lissa deGuzman and the Chicago ensemble performing an energetic “All That Jazz,” and then, a minute later, Tony nominees Sara Chase and Alex Brightman of Schmigadoon! taking over the performance space to sing that show’s opening title number (with Brightman’s spoken “I hate musicals!” joke intact.) Watch on Deadline Next, at 9:15, came Hamilton , represented her by cast member Jarrod Spector, in full regal cape and crown as King George II and singing that musical’s comic showstopper “You’ll Be Back.” Another crowd-pleaser followed (at 9:16) when Margaret Cho (in character as the narrator of The Rocky Horror Show ) led her cast mates in a rousing minute of “Let’s Do The Time Warp.” Next up were some original members of the cast of Rent , performing “Seasons of Love,” followed by LJ Benet and Maria Wirries of The Lost Boys , perched high above the street on a tower of scaffolding, performing “Now, Forever.” At 9:19 Sherri Shepherd, in full Genie regalia, was joined by Rodney Ingram as the title character from Disney’s Aladdin to sing that musical’s “Friend Like Me,” then it was quickly on to The Book of Mormon , with the dancing and singing Mormons performing the show’s signature tune “Tomorrow Is a Latter Day.” The final bit of the medley went to Wicked , with the current Broadway Elphaba (Keri René Fuller) and Glinda (Emma Flynn), performing the big number “Defying Gravity,” complete with the Wicked Witch’s very, very large, billowing black cape that would never have survived the gusts of Thanksgiving Thursday. The medley, created and choreographed by Sarah O’Gleby with composer Tom Kitt arranging the music, was a solid and affectionate attempt at honoring Broadway, though many fans and industry insiders will likely be left with a little holiday nostalgia for the days when each show got its own spotlight to perform a full musical number, like the thrilling Ragtime number last year (or last Thursday, as it turned out with the rerun) or the boundary-pushing performance from The Prom in 2018 when NBC’s cameras zoomed in on a sweet little high school prom kiss that, like today’s Saturday parade, made a bit of history itself: Emma Nolan and Alyssa Greene, the Prom ‘s ingenue stars, delivered the first same-sex kiss in parade history, to the delighted cheers and applause of the gathered spectators. ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Warms Up $83M+ Five-Day Holiday Haul Postponed Parade Kicks Off On Dry NYC Day; Broadway Gets Quick Tribute Melissa Gilbert Thanks Those Who Supported Husband Timothy Busfield David Byrne On Getting Into Character As Elon Musk For Song In ‘Musk’ Doc Read More About: Comments

title: Planning a Holiday Trip to New York City? These Hilton Hotels Put You Steps From the City’s Most Festive Attractions

There’s New York, and then there’s New York at Christmas. Few cities have played a more memorable role in holiday movies, from Kevin McCallister’s extravagant Manhattan adventure in “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York” to Buddy the Elf’s wide-eyed arrival in “Elf.” And every December, the city does a pretty convincing job of living up to its Hollywood reputation. Fifth Avenue storefronts become elaborate holiday displays, Rockefeller Center unveils its towering Christmas tree and Bryant Park transforms into a winter village complete with ice skating, holiday shopping and hot chocolate. Related Stories Spain Pitches Incentives, Crews and a 500 Million-Strong Spanish-Speaking Market to India at WAVES Film Bazaar Vinod Kapri's Himalayan Love Story 'Pyre' Heads to U.A.E., U.K. After India Release (EXCLUSIVE) Of course, the real-life version also comes with crowded sidewalks, sold-out Broadway shows and some of the most expensive hotel rooms of the year. Choosing the right place to stay can make all the difference, particularly when many of the season’s biggest attractions are within walking distance. For a holiday stay in New York City, Hilton offers several Midtown options near major seasonal attractions: The Draper New York, Tapestry Collection by Hilton, walking distance from Bryant Park’s Winter Village, New York Hilton Midtown near Rockefeller Center and Radio City Music Hall, and Tempo by Hilton New York Times Square for travelers who want to stay directly in Times Square. But make sure to book your stay directly Hilton’s website or Hilton Honors app, where travelers can access its Price Match Guarantee. Meanwhile, Hilton Honors members can take advantage of exclusive rates and earn points toward future stays. The free loyalty program also offers digital check-in, room selection and Digital Key access, allowing guests to skip the front desk and head straight to their room. Best of all, Hilton Honors Members save 20% when they book by December 22, for eligible stays through April 2, 2027. And with the More Points to Play offer, you can earn up to 3,000 Bonus Points on stays through December 31. Book now on Hilton.com or the Hilton Honors app. Terms apply. The Draper New York, Tapestry Collection by Hilton For families who prefer a little breathing room between holiday festivities, The Draper New York offers a stylish home base just far enough from the Times Square crowds. Tucked off Fifth Avenue on West 37th Street, the 143-room boutique hotel puts guests within walking distance of Bryant Park’s Winter Village, Macy’s famous holiday window displays and the Empire State Building. Part of Hilton’s Tapestry Collection, the 23-story property combines contemporary interiors with a more intimate atmosphere than Midtown’s sprawling hotels. Connecting rooms (subject to availability) allow families to stay close while giving everyone their own space to recharge after a day of sightseeing, while select accommodations feature private furnished balconies with sweeping city views. Whether the day’s plans call for an early morning of ice skating, an afternoon of Fifth Avenue shopping or an evening Broadway show, the hotel’s central location makes it easy for families to explore at their own pace — and return for a midday break when little legs need a rest. BOOK ONLINE New York Hilton Midtwon If your ideal New York Christmas itinerary involves Rockefeller Center’s famous tree, Radio City Music Hall’s Christmas Spectacular and a shopping trip along Fifth Avenue, it’s hard to beat the location of New York Hilton Midtown. The sprawling hotel sits on Sixth Avenue between West 53rd and 54th streets, directly across from the Museum of Modern Art and just two blocks from Rockefeller Center. Central Park, St. Patrick’s Cathedral and the luxury storefronts lining Fifth Avenue are also within easy walking distance. Rooms feature Hilton Serenity beds, work desks and skyline views, while select higher-floor accommodations offer glimpses of Central Park. Guests booking executive-level suites can also take advantage of the hotel’s Executive Lounge. But the hotel is also well-suited for families and larger groups, with a wide selection of guest rooms, connecting accommodations and spacious one- and two-bedroom suites. For families traveling together, connecting rooms and spacious one- and two-bedroom suites offer room to spread out without sacrificing time together — particularly welcome after a long day of sightseeing, holiday shopping and Broadway shows. Dining options are just as flexible, whether it’s a quick breakfast or grab-and-go snacks at Herb N’ Kitchen before heading out to see the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree, or cocktails and light bites at the Lobby Lounge after an evening in the city. With everything under one roof, guests can make the most of their holiday itinerary without having to plan every moment around it. Ahead of Thanksgiving, the property has another major selling point: its location directly on the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade route. The hotel also hosts a Thanksgiving buffet at Herb N’ Kitchen, featuring more than 20 dishes and over 10 desserts. However, designated parade-view rooms require multi-night stays and carry premium rates, so booking early is particularly important. title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Kicks Off, Making History On A Dry And Breezy Saturday
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Kicks Off, Making History On A Dry And Breezy Saturday ‘The Hunting Wives’ Pays Tribute To Lionsgate Exec Salli Newman Justin Timberlake Visits Jimmy Fallon And Shares Thanksgiving Dish On New Apple TV Doc Series, How David Bowie Influenced ‘SexyBack’ & Performs Dance Classics View All November 28, 2026 5:51am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The giant balloons are ready to make history today Kena Betancur/Getty Images With New York City temperatures in the mid-40s with some light breezes and no rain, the postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade got underway this morning at 8:30 a.m. ET, making history as the first such parade to make its way through Manhattan in the event’s 100 year history. Two of this year’s hosts, NBC’s Savannah Guthrie and Hoda Kotb, welcomed viewers, calling the event historic and unprecedented. Guthrie said, “To the city, to the volunteers, to the crews and performers and the more than 11,000 people who made this parade happen and insisted upon it, thank you. You made sure that not only would the show go on but that it would be every bit as spectacular as the 100th deserves.” Related Stories News Broadway Gets Speed-Dating-Style Tribute At Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade News The Show Must Go On: Broadway Will Perform Saturday In Macy's Thanksgiving Parade “Every balloon, float, every surprise,” Guthrie continued, “is still on, and because it is the parade is the 100th some iconic inflatables are coming out of the archives for the first time in decades.” (One of those classics is the ’60s cartoon character Underdog.) Watch on Deadline British singer-songwriter Raye along with her sisters Amma and Absolutely got things off to a musical start, performing just before the parade itself stepped off. Paddington the Bear – apparently the costumed performer/remote-control puppet hybrid that appears in the upcoming Paddington Broadway musical – made an early appearance, chatting with Guthrie and Kodb in the interview area (the bear will return later atop its own parade float.) Postponed from Thursday due to severe weather – torrential rains, high winds – that would have endangered participants and spectators (and certainly would have grounded the giant floating balloons that are a cherished element of the event) the parade is expected to include nearly all of the performers, marching bands and Broadway shows that were initially planned. The parade will be broadcast on NBC and will stream on Peacock. There were some last-minute changes: At least two marching bands, including The Macy’s Great American Marching Band, the annual ensemble of high school musicians from across the country, and University of Alabama’s Million Dollar Band, which returned home to perform at the annual Alabama-Auburn matchup known as the Iron Bowl. And while Macy’s has not at this writing released an official parade line-up, organizers previously noted that 95% of the line-up initially scheduled for Thursday would be on hand today, with two newcomers – LL Cool J and Gloria Gaynor – added to the linup. That original lineup included Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Queen Latifah, Keke Palmer, JoJo and Jimmy Fallon & The Roots, as well as a tribute to Dolly Parton led by Megan Hilty, and special appearances by Melissa Joan Hart, Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer and Holly Robinson Peete. Newly added Gaynor is expected to sing her signature song “I Will Survive.” According to Macy’s last year’s parade – the broadcast of which was rerun on Thursday – drew about 3.5 million in-person spectators, and a similar number is expected today. What Macy’s is calling the “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” will go on as planned, with performers from The Lost Boys, The Rocky Horror Show, Wicked, Schmigadoon!, Aladdin, The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Hamiilton and the 30th-anniversary tribute to Rent taking part in the first-of-its-kind, 14-minute Broadway medley (traditionally, the participating Broadway shows perform on their own, one at a time.) Paddington the Musical is confirmed to participate in the Saturday broadcast as a separate float, as originally intended. As for those high school and college marching bands that each year travel from around the country to participate in the parade, this year’s participants had to scramble to make the travel and hotel accommodations – and raise the necessary funding – necessitated by the delay. And nearly all seem to have done so successfully: The last few days saw the schools’ local communities and sponsors step up to help cover the costs, and just today Macy’s announced that it is donating $50,000 to the music program of every school band in the parade to defray this year’s costs. (Various bands have been posting on social media about their efforts to raise the tens and even hundreds of thousands of dollars needed for an additional couple days in New York City.) As for that delay, while Thursday’s weather began reasonably mild – prompting some keyboard critics to question the decision to delay, and some MAGA types criticizing New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani for pulling the plug – the feared storm most certainly did arrive by late morning Thursday, and continued to intensify through the day, causing flooding, downed trees and electrical outages throughout the New York City area. Macy’s has been especially careful with the giant balloons after a 1998 incident in which an inflatable Cat in the Hat was blown off course by gusts and smashed into a lamppost, sending a large piece of metal tumbling into the crowd of spectators, injuring four people, including a woman who spent nearly a month in a coma. ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ Warms Up $83M+ Five-Day Holiday Haul Postponed Parade Kicks Off On Dry NYC Day; Broadway Gets Quick Tribute Melissa Gilbert Thanks Those Who Supported Husband Timothy Busfield The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion Worldwide Read More About: 1 Comments

title: A Demon Baby and a Contract-Killing Company Anchor Indonesian Dark Comedy ‘Gokill’ at JAFF Market

Their joy turns to desperation when doctors discover that their unborn child is unlikely to survive. The couple turns to black magic, binding Sugeng to Silly, a demon baby that feeds on human organs. To save their unborn child, they must help Silly grow into adulthood. Related Stories Skydance Q3 Profit Powered By Studios, Streaming 'GTA 6' Presales 'Far in Excess' of Expectations Ahead of Next Week's Launch, Take-Two CEO Says As Sugeng struggles to keep up with the demon baby’s appetite, he discovers that the cleaning company he works for, Gokill, harbors a dark secret: it also operates a contract-killing division. Writer-director Amanda Iswan made her directorial debut with “Zeta: When the Dead Awaken” (2019). “I’ve always been fascinated by how easily love can become the perfect excuse for doing terrible things,” Iswan says. “What I find interesting about dark comedy is that we can find ourselves laughing at situations we would normally find disturbing, or sympathizing with characters whose actions we would normally condemn.” A short film of the same title, also written, directed and produced by Iswan, screened at the 2025 Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival . The feature project, however, develops a distinct premise centered on the demon baby and Gokill’s hidden operations. “What excites me about ‘Gokill’ is how it takes this very real economic anxiety and explores it through an absurd supernatural premise,” producers James Erlangga, Damar Ardi and Aufa Ariaputra tell Variety . “Despite its fantastical elements, Sugeng’s struggles are something many people experience in their everyday lives.” “Gokill” previously received the Pitching Forum MTN Development Grant and the BSM Premiere Gear Fund at Jakarta Film Week 2026. The project is currently in development under Angin Segar Films, Kapsul Waktu Studio and Satu Atap, with Iswan refining the screenplay and shaping the film’s creative and visual direction. “Our main goal at JAFF Market is to secure funding and find the right partners to move ‘Gokill’ from development toward production,” the producers say. “Beyond financing, we’re also interested in exploring the film’s potential in the international market. We believe ‘Gokill’ has a distinctive premise and universal themes that can resonate with audiences beyond Indonesia.” JAFF Market, the industry arm of the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival, runs Nov. 28–30 at the Jogja Expo Center in Yogyakarta. Li Latest Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival Opens With Lawrence Fajardo’s ‘Silenced Nights’ and a Call to Face Reality 1 hour ago Indonesian Social Thriller ‘A Quiet Sunshine’ Speaks Up for Women’s Bodily Autonomy at JAFF Market 6 hours ago Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or Winner ‘Fjord’ Takes Jakarta World Cinema Audience Award as Short Film Winners Land Debut Feature Funding 3 weeks ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Australian director Rosie Lourde’s debut project “ Wreck and Ruin ” is being presented at the 2026 JAFF Future Project at JAFF Market . Set in 1893 on a tropical volcanic island with black-sand coastlines, the story follows Elizabeth, who has just lost her sister Christina in a shipwreck, as she falls in love with Louis. Related Stories Wacom and India's IICT Ink Pact at IFFI Goa With Scholarships, Manga and Anime Masterclasses 'Ramayana' Star Sai Pallavi, Ravi Kishan's 'Spider-Man' Anecdote, Grammy Winner Ricky Kej Light Up International Film Festival of India Opening in Goa Written by Katharine McPhee, who is also a producer on the project, the script turns the classic story of love as salvation on its head and asks: what happens when the lover doesn’t want to be saved, but only wants to possess the other? “I was drawn to the visceral tension of Katharine taking the classic fairy tale of ‘ Beauty and the Beast ‘ and flipping it into a survival thriller about coercive control,” Lourde tells Variety . “Setting that psychological trap against little-known Australian maritime history across the Indonesian archipelago felt electric, visually stunning and timely.” The $2.5 million project is in advanced development with a polished draft of the script, and is designed to combine on-location production in Indonesia with Australian grants and post-production. For McPhee, the script is a passion project she has been personally committed to for several years. “I believe in its strong commercial appeal as a genre film, as well as its timely story and themes,” McPhee tells Variety. “The attachment of Rosie as director and producer has bolstered the project. I’m so excited to see it continue to evolve as an enticing project in today’s marketplace.” At JAFF Market, the team hopes to connect with equity financiers, regional buyers and key production partners. Alongside “Wreck and Ruin,” Lourde is executive producing Nick Annas’ “Crashout,” which will world premiere at an A-list U.S. festival in early 2027. title: Indonesian Social Thriller ‘A Quiet Sunshine’ Speaks Up for Women’s Bodily Autonomy at JAFF Market
full_text: × Nov 28, 2026 3:45am PT Indonesian Social Thriller ‘A Quiet Sunshine’ Speaks Up for Women’s Bodily Autonomy at JAFF Market By Jenny S. Li Plus Icon Jenny S. Li Latest Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival Opens With Lawrence Fajardo’s ‘Silenced Nights’ and a Call to Face Reality 52 minutes ago ‘Beauty and the Beast’ Becomes a Tale of Coercive Control in Romantic Thriller ‘Wreck and Ruin’ at JAFF Market 5 hours ago Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or Winner ‘Fjord’ Takes Jakarta World Cinema Audience Award as Short Film Winners Land Debut Feature Funding 3 weeks ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source QUN Films Indonesian writer-director Ninndi Raras’ debut project “ A Quiet Sunshine ” is among the projects selected for the 2026 JAFF Future Project at JAFF Market . The story follows the intuitive bond between two women living on a remote Indonesian island: Melyana, a midwife, and Amira, a 17-year-old who became pregnant as a result of a sexual assault. Facing a fleeting 14-week legal abortion window and an unsupportive social system, they decide to escape the island in search of freedom. Related Stories A.R. Rahman Unpacks His Hindustani Classical Score for Bharat Bala's IFFI-Selected Maha Kumbh Drama 'Banaras' AI Films From Kerala to the Andaman Islands Set for WIF India x Google Flow Filmathon, Screen at IFFI Goa (EXCLUSIVE) “I want to show a quiet act of resistance. Melyana and Amira aren’t trying to change the world. They simply break the rules to build a safe space and reclaim their own bodies. I hope the audience walks away feeling the power of that quiet solidarity,” Raras tells Variety . The project stems from Raras’ own experience of sexual assault as a teenager. Years later, she went through pregnancy herself. “If a consensual pregnancy already demands so much, what happens when a woman is forced to carry a child without consent? Her own body becomes an uninvited collaborator,” she says. Raras, the mother of a daughter, is concerned that systemic inequality that can strip women of autonomy is deeply embedded around the world. “I want [my daughter] to grow up in a world where she is never a victim of this system, and where she always owns her body,” the director says. Giovanni Rahmadeva of QUN Films boarded the project as a producer because “it captures that exact clash between society’s loud, suffocating outrage and the quiet, unshakeable calm of women reclaiming their own bodies.” Rahmadeva values the role of midwives as a symbol of women caring for and protecting one another under male-dominated power. “Sharing women’s real stories isn’t just a gesture; it’s the core of our creative mission. Based on true events, this story brings forward truths that are often silenced by strict traditions,” says Rahmadeva. Backed by QUN Films and Catchlight Pictures, the project is at the advanced script stage and aims to move into pre-production and shooting by mid-2027. At JAFF Market, the team is looking to meet international co-producers, sales agents and distributors to close the financing gap. title: Migrant Worker Tale ‘Luz and Flor’ Finds Prehistoric Filipino and Indonesian Humans in Spain at JAFF Market
full_text: × Nov 28, 2026 3:35am PT Migrant Worker Tale ‘Luz and Flor’ Finds Prehistoric Filipino and Indonesian Humans in Spain at JAFF Market By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Migrant Worker Tale ‘Luz and Flor’ Finds Prehistoric Filipino and Indonesian Humans in Spain at JAFF Market 6 hours ago Indonesian Body Horror ‘Primal’ Turns a Mother’s Grief Monstrous at JAFF Market 6 hours ago Indonesian Cinema’s Next Chapter Is Reaching the World ‘Without Losing Our Cultural Identity,’ Says JAFF Market Director Linda Gozali 12 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Katalog Two prehistoric humans, one from the Philippines and one from Indonesia, cross paths as laborers in Spain in “ Luz and Flor ,” the new feature project from Filipino filmmaker Glenn Barit (“Cleaners”). The project, also known as “Luzonensis and Floresiensis,” is among the 2026 JAFF Future Project selections at JAFF Market . With Spain’s property market collapsing around them, the pair look for a place to belong and a way to get by, while the echoes of colonial rule go unresolved. Related Stories Indie Filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar Look to 'Dangal' China Playbook, Pop-Up Cinemas and Screening Fees to Find Audiences 'Godavari' Director Nikhil Mahajan Turns a Malegaon Carjacking Into Neo-Noir With WAVES Film Bazaar Project 'Mongoose' The project was recently selected for the International Film Festival Rotterdam’s CineMart 2027 and won the Talents Tokyo Award in 2025. It took part in the QCinema Project Market in Quezon City, Philippines, in 2025, and has been through the West Meets East Screenplay Lab 2026 in Dhaka, the Film Development Council of the Philippines’ Isapelikula Script Lab in Manila and the AFANxPaS Young Filmmakers Bootcamp 2026, held in Manila, Bangkok and Paris. “When I was young, I used to frequent the caves where the bones of the Homo luzonensis were discovered. It is known to be the earliest ancient human species in the Philippines,” Barit says. “So I became curious about this caveman character and the history that he might carry and represent.” A 2023 trip to Jogja, as Yogyakarta is known, left Barit struck by how alike Filipinos and Indonesians are, and how different. “I feel like we are two nations blurred by modern ideas of nations and borders,” he says. Homo luzonensis is also thought to be a close relative of Homo floresiensis, a species found on Indonesia’s Flores Island. Barit wanted to drop the two characters into present-day struggles, as migrants in countries that once ruled their own. “I’m curious about these intersections as well as their ironies. How these supposedly ‘primitive’ figures might have something to say about our modern world,” he says. “It also just seems exciting to research about and a bit funny to shoot.” He is aiming for a tone that is thoughtful but playful. “Maybe a way of interrogating serious and tough questions through something absurd and imaginative,” Barit says. The film is produced by Kristine De Leon of the Philippines and Tanveer Hossain of Bangladesh through their company Katalog. The feature grows out of Barit’s short “Luzonensis Osteoporosis,” which played festivals abroad. “Glenn Barit has an extraordinary ability to tell stories that feel fresh, inventive, and distinctly his own, without ever chasing trends,” De Leon says. “Tanveer Hossain and I were immediately drawn to the short film. We found it beautifully crafted, thoughtfully directed, and full of creative possibilities.” The pair worked together for several years before setting up Katalog. “As producers from the Philippines and Bangladesh, we believe in bringing filmmakers and creative voices from different countries together through meaningful co-productions,” De Leon says. “‘Luz and Flor’ is a wonderful example of this vision.” The screenplay is in its second draft, with the next draft underway, and the team is preparing for more research, notably in Spain, along with further creative consultations. Financing is planned for next year. At JAFF Market, the producers hope to bring Indonesian talent on board – a co-producer, a writing partner and a performer – to give the story’s Indonesian side authenticity. They are also courting funders, sales agents and festival programmers. Barit, meanwhile, is preparing a short backed by the Film Development Council of the Philippines that he will shoot 50 times, each time with a different cast, and is in early development on a romance feature about pet custody. title: Channel 4 Defends Huw Edwards Doc After Government Criticism: “There Is Clear Public Interest In Confronting Him With Questions”
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Netflix Edits Schizophrenia Scene Out Of Tyson Fury Doc After Wife Reveals Boxer Does Not Have Condition International Insider: Doha Days; Tricky Week For BAFTA; ‘Remarried Empress’ Interview Canal+ Sends Signal To African Creative Community With Academy Launch Backed By President Of South Africa View All November 28, 2026 2:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Former BBC News anchor Huw Edwards outside court in London, July 2024. Dan Kitwood/Getty Images Channel 4 has been forced to defend its Huw Edwards doc three days before it premieres, with the network’s news chief saying the film has “clear public interest.” Channel 4 unveiled Huw Edwards – Guilty last week and it will air Tuesday night. It has already been met with a barrage of criticism including from the upper echelons of UK government . News chief Louisa Compton issued a rare and lengthy statement this morning, saying: “We understand that some people will profoundly disagree with our decision to make this film. But discomfort is not, in itself, a reason for journalism not to ask difficult questions. We believe those questions are in the public interest.” Related Stories News BBC Being Investigated Over Antisemitism By Government Adviser News Huw Edwards To Speak On TV For First Time About Criminal Actions & Fall From Grace In Channel 4 Doc The statement came after the Prime Minister’s spokesperson said the country has “no interest in hearing what [Edwards] has to say,” while paying tribute to the “victims of child sexual abuse and exploitation.” Watch on Deadline Compton joined with government in saying that behind Edwards’ offences are “real children and real victims – including those as young as seven – who have been abused.” But she stressed that the disgraced ex- BBC News anchor “is not being allowed to tell his story unchallenged or on his own terms,” and was not paid or given editorial control. “Journalism isn’t about only putting people on television whose actions or opinions we approve of,” she added. “Sometimes its purpose is precisely the opposite: to look directly at people who have done terrible things, confront them with difficult questions, test their explanations and allow audiences to judge what they say for themselves.” Compton, who was recently promoted to Director of News, Digital and Audience Trust, said the doc “raises wider and uncomfortable questions about power, trust and accountability, and about how our criminal justice system responds to people convicted of offences involving indecent images of children.” Airing on Tuesday night, the doc will be the first time Edwards has spoken publicly on TV about his conviction and fall from grace. He has addressed his actions on his Substack but this will be the first time he speaks about them with an interviewer. A short trailer sees Edwards say “I’d lost the plot” after being questioned over why he did what he did. The interviewer can then be heard saying exasperatedly, “Oh, come on.” Allegations of grooming and paying younger people for sexually explicit images were published about Edwards in 2023 by The Sun and the following year he pled guilty to making indecent images of children. He has since mostly retreated from public life, returning to where he grew up in Wales, which is where the doc takes place. Compton’s statement in full “It is reasonable to ask why Channel 4 has made this film, and why now. As a public service broadcaster, we have a responsibility to think very carefully about what we put on screen, balancing the public interest in asking difficult questions of powerful people against the potential impact on our audiences, and particularly on victims and survivors of abuse. We did not take that decision lightly. Journalism isn’t about only putting people on television whose actions or opinions we approve of. Sometimes its purpose is precisely the opposite: to look directly at people who have done terrible things, confront them with difficult questions, test their explanations and allow audiences to judge what they say for themselves. The circumstances and gravity are of course very different, but journalists routinely interview and hold to account people who have committed dreadful acts, including murderers, terrorists and dictators. The principle is the same: interviewing someone is not an endorsement of them. It is an opportunity to challenge what they have done, interrogate their account and allow audiences to judge their answers for themselves. That is what this film does. Huw Edwards is not being allowed to tell his story unchallenged or on his own terms. He is questioned throughout by an experienced director; he was not paid; he had no control over the content of the film; and there were no restrictions on the questions he could be asked. Edwards was one of the most prominent and trusted broadcasters in Britain. He pleaded guilty to serious offences involving indecent images of children and has never publicly faced detailed questioning about his criminal behaviour or the complete collapse of his career and reputation. There is a clear public interest in confronting him with those questions rather than allowing them to remain unanswered. We are also acutely conscious that behind offences involving indecent images are real children and real victims – including those as young as seven – who have been abused. Nothing about making this film diminishes the seriousness of that harm, nor does Edwards’ participation entitle him to sympathy, redemption or rehabilitation. His account is there to be tested, not accepted. Channel 4’s remit is also to stimulate debate. This film raises wider and uncomfortable questions about power, trust and accountability, and about how our criminal justice system responds to people convicted of offences involving indecent images of children. Those questions extend far beyond one disgraced public figure and deserve serious scrutiny. Channel 4 has a long and established record of investigating powerful figures and confronting serious wrongdoing. That same journalistic instinct applies here: holding people to account sometimes means investigating them from the outside, and sometimes it means gaining access, challenging them directly and testing the account they give of their actions. We should be capable of examining difficult issues rather than looking away because we don’t like what we see. We understand that some people will profoundly disagree with our decision to make this film. But discomfort is not, in itself, a reason for journalism not to ask difficult questions. He was 38. Haley died Friday following medical complications, the WWE announced. No further details were reported. “Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE . But more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague,” the WWE shared in an Instagram post. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife Paige, their daughter, as well as all his friends, co-workers and fans.” Related Stories Movies Gerald R. In an interview with the New York Times , Greenblatt admitted that it’s easier to be a producer on an old hit that’s enjoying a second life in streaming than it is to launch “a whole new show to the marketplace.” “We’re still being pummeled by new shows on every streaming service and rather than try to figure out what’s worth committing to, it’s easier to just escape into Seinfeld or Downtown Abbey because you know exactly what you’re getting,” said Greenblatt, who’s currently an EP on The Gilded Age. Greenblatt’s comments were included in a story about the growing popularity of old TV hits on platforms like Netflix and Amazon Prime. Luminate reports that viewership of old titles during this year’s third quarter increased more than 40 percent among the major streaming services, compared with the same period last year. Tune in for new TV series and movies declined during that same time. Watch on Deadline Netflix continues to demonstrate that old shows can be new and popular again with today’s subscribers. title: Strong ‘I Play Rocky,’ ‘How to Rob a Bank’ KO and More: Amazon MGM Distribution Head on 2026 Highs and Lows
full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All November 27, 2026 6:49pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Anthony Ippolito in 'I Play Rocky.' Claire Folger/Amazon MGM Studios Amazon MGM Studios ‘ team is relishing the thrill of the theatrical fight as I Play Rocky looks to capitalize on its muscular start. Peter Farrelly’s fact-based underdog drama stars Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone amid his battle in the 1970s to get his script for Rocky into production with himself in the lead role. After two weekends in limited release, I Play Rocky rose to No. 2 at the domestic box office as it expanded wide last weekend. It is expected to gross roughly $9 million for the five-day Thanksgiving frame, which would bring its North American cume to around $22 million through Sunday. Related Stories Movies Denis Villeneuve Pledges Traditional, "Unapologetic" Bond: "Not Here to Change the DNA" Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Devouring $85M Over Thanksgiving Weekend as 'Focker-in-Law,' 'Hexed' Launch I Play Rocky is the latest release in a buzzy year for the studio, following the mammoth success of this spring’s Project Hail Mary — set for rerelease Dec. 11 as awards season comes out swinging — and a winning path for Verity . Amazon MGM also sparked recent conversation with its unusual release plan for Sacha Baron Cohen’s Ali G: Who Iz I? , which received a two-day theatrical run just before hitting Prime Video, and for its tough turnout for David Leitch’s How to Rob a Bank , the $40 million-budgeted heist film that opened earlier this month with just $5.1 million domestically . During a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter conducted ahead of Thanksgiving, Amazon MGM head of domestic theatrical distribution Kevin Wilson shares insight into I Play Rocky’ s broad appeal and the hopes that it continues to find younger audiences after that impressive A+ CinemaScore . Wilson also weighs in on the releases for How to Rob a Bank , Ali G and David O. Russell’s Madden , not to mention the company’s big James Bond casting news . Anthony Ippolito and Stephan James in I Play Rocky. Claire Folger/Amazon Content Services How are you feeling with I Play Rocky now playing wide? It’s a great start. From the first time we saw the movie — and really from the first time I read the script — I knew we had a special story. What Pete [Farrelly] and the filmmaking team were able to put on screen, coupled with Anthony Ippolito’s performance, we got magic. As we went [wide last] weekend, we saw the audience response, which is always good just to validate our own intuition. With that A+ CinemaScore and a 97 percent in the top two boxes [on PostTrak] and an 88 definite recommend, we always hoped that this thing would have legs. We’re pretty confident. The movie was the subject of Oscar talk ever since premiering at TIFF. Something we’re consistently seeing is the ability of Anthony to portray Sly, [and] that is not the easiest character in the world to play. It’s one of those feel-good, perseverance stories that doesn’t come around that often. The unique thing about this one is, we rolled it out, and we saw good numbers in New York and L.A. and, of course, Philly, but it’s interesting to see [now that it’s wide]. I’m not super surprised, but the movie’s playing broad from a geographical standpoint. It’s playing solid across the country. We’ve got theaters in Redlands, California, in the top 10 — Goodyear, Arizona [and] Santa Clarita [in California]. It’s performing really well in the South Central part of the country and those Texas regions. We are getting a nice percentage of the Hispanic audience in. I know that Hollywood loves movies about Hollywood, but it’s sometimes hard to predict if broad audiences will, too. I think it just goes to [show], these are Rocky fans. They’re fans of Sly, and they’re fans of the Rocky franchise. We’re definitely playing a little bit older right now, which is not a surprise — 53 percent of our audience is 45-plus [as of last weekend]. As we get into Thanksgiving, the hope is that maybe that age playability comes down a little bit. I do think it could be one of those Thanksgiving films in the marketplace that’s a good choice for adult families to all agree on a movie. Anna Sawai and Nicholas Hoult in How to Rob a Bank . Courtesy of Amazon MGM Studios Another movie focusing on a public figure and sparking social buzz is Madden . Was there talk of putting that one in theaters? That movie was always greenlit as a streaming movie. That was always the plan, to release it in that Thanksgiving corridor at home for audiences. Christian Bale’s performance is unbelievable in that movie. Speaking of Rocky, your year got off to a great start with Project Hail Mary , which continues to be part of the Oscar conversation. We’re really excited. I came over from the MGM team, so I’ve always been releasing theatrical movies. But it’s our first big year at Amazon MGM putting a pretty robust slate together, and to have that movie pop the way it did early on in this theatrical journey, obviously, was a really good thing. Between [directors] Chris [Miller] and Phil [Lord] and [star] Ryan [Gosling], what they were able to put on screen was really something special. We’re rereleasing it back in theaters on Dec. 11th, and we’ll have some IMAX screens and back in 70mm in locations. Just get that audience back out to see it in a theater where it deserves to be seen. We’ll see what happens. Lionel Boyce and Ryan Gosling in Project Hail Mary. Jonathan Olley/Amazon Content Services Any thoughts on what happened with How to Rob a Bank ? Tough one. Obviously, not what we were hoping for and certainly not what our expectations were [with] releasing this film theatrically. It’s a tough marketplace. That’s the unique thing about the marketplace right now, is there’s no floor on these movies. It was tough to connect with a younger audience on this movie, and we’re still trying to figure it out a little bit internally, why this thing didn’t at least click for that younger audience in a bigger way. Have you seen the movie? Yeah, fun one and big David Leitch fan. The movie’s fun. Nick [Hoult] and Pete [Davidson] and that crew, it’s fun to watch, but then Zoë [Kravitz] and John C. Reilly, that relationship is really good in the movie. It’s a little bit of a head-scratcher, and we’re still living in that world where the theatrical hurdle is not small. Trying to convince audiences to get off their couch, to get off YouTube, to get off all the streaming services — it’s not an easy thing to do. For this particular movie, it was just tough to get audiences into a theater. The unique thing about Amazon MGM, comparative to some other studios — and it’s not an excuse or deflecting the underperformance theatrically — but we have the second biggest streaming platform on the planet. The life cycle of our films are a little bit different than other studios. So I’m really hopeful that that’s where audiences are going to find this movie. How did the team decide on the unique strategy for Ali G: Who Iz I? , with just the two-day theatrical run? We always wanted to do some sort of a theatrical event with that movie. That was always the plan. We know he has this rabid fan base, so we wanted to create an event in theaters. We decided just to do that two-night event in theaters and then get it to Prime Video as quickly as possible. It’s just like we’ve seen with the Jackass movie and some of these other comps: That theatrical hurdle is just tough. To convince a really wide audience that they need to go see a film like that in theaters is not the easiest thing to do. We came up with that event-style release and got it to Prime Video as quickly as we could, and the performance on Prime Video has been solid. Robert Pattinson as James Bond for Amazon MGM Studios. Jaap Buitendijk Your team certainly dominated headlines recently with Robert Pattinson’s casting as Bond. Super, super excited for that one. I got to release No Time to Die , which is Daniel [Craig’s] last movie [as Bond]. This one’s going to be really fun — a reinvention of the franchise, and it’ll be super interesting as this cast starts to fill out. Absolutely. I’ve gone full circle with Rob Pattinson. I was at Summit Entertainment and released the Twilight movies way back in the day. God, I think he was 17 at the time. It’s been a fun journey to see his career, and now his Bond will be great. THR

title: Donald Trump Jr.’s Outrage Gifts Netflix’s ‘Hunting Wives’ Some Priceless Streisand Effect PR
full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Donald Trump Jr.’s Outrage Gifts Netflix’s ‘Hunting Wives’ Some Priceless Streisand Effect PR Trump’s “Noisy Name-Calling” Mocked By NYT After Bored POTUS Starts Thanksgiving Ranting Against Reporter’s Nvidia Dispatch Bono Bowl Review: U2 Delivers Halftime Goods & Hits On Netflix & NFL’s First Thanksgiving Eve Game, With A Little Help From Dolly Parton View All November 27, 2026 3:46pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Hunting Wives' ; Donald Trump Jr Netflix/Getty Images Christmas came on Thanksgiving for Netflix ‘s The Hunting Wives , thanks to a fatuous Donald Trump Jr. Never slow to put his silver foot in his big mouth, the oldest and most ambitious son of El Presidente got very hot under the digital collar early on Turkey Day over a passionate promo for the soapy and streamy MAGA-themed series of two women kissing. In proclaiming “What is wrong with you??? It’s Thanksgiving” on X on November 26 in reply to Netflix, the no stranger to controversy and speculation Don Jr. looks to have handed the Season 2 launch of the Rebecca Cutter-created show the kind of publicity even Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters ‘ well-funded team can’t buy. Related Stories News 'The Hunting Wives' Pays Tribute To Lionsgate Exec Salli Newman News Federal Incentive Will Level The Playing Field For America's Creatives -- Guest Column What is wrong with you??? It’s Thanksgiving. — Donald Trump Jr. (@DonaldJTrumpJr) November 26, 2026 While the First Louche’s outrage may have struck some as reeking of hypocrisy, or at least lacking all self-awareness, the fact is Don Jr’s tweet has been viewed over 7.5 million times since Thanksgiving morning. Add to that, a flood of media coverage from the highbrow to the gutter press and (we see you Fox News) everything in-between and you have yourself a good old fashion water cooler moment. Watch on Deadline Starring Brittany Snow and Malin Åkerman as Sophie and Margo, an East Coast newcomer to an East Texas town and the town’s leading lady, The Hunting Wives is based on the May Cobb novel of the same name. With guns, booze, short leather skirts, cowboy boots, MAGA , murder and lots of sex, the show follows Sophie as she loses more and more of her old Boston life and becomes more intimate with the scheming Margo, whose Dermot Mulroney -portrayed oil tycoon husband is running for Lone Star state governor. Hunting Wives scribe Brandon Zuck took out a shiv of his own against Don Jr. on Instagram, as well as delivering a backhanded compliment. “Just wait until season 3,” he wrote on his IG Story next to a screenshot of Junior’s tweet. That echoes what Cutter said when Netflix announced Season 3 last month. “Buckle up, because Season 3 will be even more scandalous and twisted,” the showrunner stated. Further add to Jr’s ill-considered pearl clutching, the fact the actual online clip of Snow and Åkerman’s characters making out has itself claimed 36 million views on the (MAGA? Not MAGA ?) Elon Musk -owned platform. All of which means the Streisand effect of Little Don’s post cannot have been helpful in pushing Hunting Wives Season 2’s eight episode debt to number #3 in the Netflix charts in less than 24 hours. Likely not wanting to throw cold water on a good firestorm, Netflix did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment on Little Don’s tweet and the backlash it’s received. But, why would they? As WME Ari’s brother, former White House Chief of Staff and budding 2028 candidate Rahm Emanuel once said: “You never want a serious crisis to go to waste.” The seriousness of it all aside, for a streamer that has been short of late of big breakout hits , Don Jr’s foot-stamping may have proved the spark to set the already well-watched Hunting Wives on fire — in the best way. Or as Netflix posted on their official feed later on Thanksgiving: “It’s messy is what it is!” Happy Thanksgiving? pic.twitter.com/NgWf2lPaAS — Netflix (@netflix) November 26, 2026 BTW – The Streisand effect comes from the superstar taking photographer Kenneth Adelman to court for $50 million in 2003 for a pic he took of her Malibu home. Barely noticed before the lawsuit, the photo became widely viewed in the aftermath — thereby destroying the whole point of the Funny Girl star’s effort. title: NBC Pulls Ad Criticizing U.S. Military Aid to Israel After Backlash, Reviews Approval Process
full_text: × Skip to main content By THR Staff Plus Icon THR Staff View All November 27, 2026 3:41pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source IMEU Policy Project ad Courtesy Youtube/IMEU Policy Project NBC will not air a controversial anti-Israel advertisement again after it drew backlash for airing during Wednesday night’s Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special. A person familiar with the situation told The Hollywood Reporter that senior management was unaware of the advertisement until after it aired. NBCUniversal will now evaluate its advertising approval process to ensure appropriate levels of review. The 30-second advertisement, titled “Every Three Seconds,” shows a young girl saving money for a year by doing yard work, including mowing the lawn, blowing leaves and shoveling snow, until she raises $400 to buy a bicycle. The ad then cuts to a girl in Gaza, standing on crutches and missing a leg amid rubble, as the narrator draws a comparison between the two scenarios and U.S. military aid to Israel. Related Stories Business NBC Uses Thanksgiving TV to Kickstart 2028 LA Olympics Marketing Push TV Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed as Storm Descends on Northeast “Over a year, she saved $400 for a new bicycle,” the voiceover says. It then cuts to the girl in Gaza. “Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this.” The advertisement was paid for by the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project, or IMEU Policy Project. This pro-Palestinian advocacy nonprofit supports ending U.S. military aid to Israel. The group’s campaign, titled “No More for Israel,” encourages viewers to contact their congressional representatives to oppose continued military assistance to the country. After the advertisement aired, several Jewish and pro-Israel organizations criticized NBC for broadcasting the spot. Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt criticized the network in a post on X, writing , “Again and again, why do people in positions of authority fail to demonstrate basic decency, let alone respect, for the Jewish community? At a moment of escalating antisemitism, there is no rationale to justify fanning the flames with such a twisted narrative.” B’nai B’rith International also condemned the advertisement in a Facebook post. “Shame on NBC,” the nonprofit wrote . “The suffering of innocent civilians is a tragedy. But using a child’s pain to spread a twisted, one-sided story that blames the Jewish state, and by extension Jews everywhere, is disgusting.” Jim Berk, CEO of the Simon Wiesenthal Center, also shared a statement with THR criticizing the network for airing the advertisement. “The advertisement’s imagery, an American child’s hardship set against the anguish of a child in Gaza, offers viewers a seductive but unsubstantiated narrative: that the struggles of American families are somehow bound up with U.S. support for Israel,” the statement reads in part. “In collapsing a complex foreign policy into a single, emotionally charged imagery, erases the deeper realities, including the imperative to protect Israeli lives and the very existence of the country itself. By manipulating emotion and stripping it of context, this ad seeks to become a catalyst for hostility.” THR
